summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent left leg cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, lipodermatosclerosis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted due to worsening erythema, pain, and swelling in her left leg over the prior 24 hours. She had recently discontinued doxycycline after outpatient improvement, but symptoms recurred. IV vancomycin was initiated, and pain was managed with oxycodone after a morphine allergy reaction. She remained afebrile with stable labs and improving clinical signs. Imaging ruled out necrotizing infection, septic joint, and DVT. The rash that developed on admission was attributed to contact dermatitis. She transitioned to oral doxycycline at discharge with plans for infectious disease follow-up, and was advised to continue compression, elevation, and all chronic medications including iron supplementation and Creon. She was discharged home in stable condition.
